extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) + codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF. Execution is deferred to the next round per the task contract (generation only; this round also ran no compile check).
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables; @kind problem requires the element+message two-column select) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist).
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index carrying the path/value; parameter position including the self slot for param/file_api_def rows; -1 when the receiver or the return value carries it)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO source or sink row is expected to resolve at API level: the file-access channels flow through bare module names (os, os.path, io, shelve, tarfile, zipfile, mmap, imp) and instance members on local variables (settings_path, tracker_path, archive, client, history_file_name, cache_path) that API graphs cannot bind to stdlib members, and os/pathlib/shelve/tarfile/zipfile are not part of the database (only the thefuck tree is). The column is kept 'ast' for all families for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, os/os.environ/known_args/command conventions). Member-name matching (.open/.exists/.is_dir/.joinpath/.expanduser/...) is receiver-name-agnostic on purpose: receiver identity cannot be proven syntactically (a .open()/.exists() on a non-path object would be a name-collision row); receiver hints (settings_path/tracker_path/path/archive/client/...) are emitted for the labeling step. The os.path.* families additionally require the syntactic `os.path.` receiver chain, and the environ families require the `os.environ.` chain, which removes the common false shapes.

All rows are candidate-grade: the broad command_output/command_script families are intentionally recall-first (the failed command's output IS the tool's payload; the labeling step filters rules whose output never reaches a path).

uncoveredCases: Rule modules are loaded dynamically via imp.load_source (types.py:144) and invoked dynamically (rule.match(command) at types.py:181, rule.get_new_command at :193, side_effect(old_cmd, script) at types.py:255): CodeQL cannot resolve these calls, so per-rule dataflow into match(command)/get_new_command(command) parameters would not connect to the entrypoint boundary. The extraction compensates by emitting the CONSUMPTION-side reads (command.output / command.script_parts attribute reads inside each rule file) as source rows, which is why those two families are broad.

command.script (full command string) and command.stdout/.stderr (deprecated properties) reads are NOT emitted: command.script feeds corrected-command string construction (primarily a command-injection channel for a later pass; script_parts is the argv-level view that feeds the path checks), and .stdout/.stderr only appear on Popen results (proc.stdout at apt_invalid_operation.py:46, dnf_no_such_command.py:26, docker_not_command.py:25, gem_unknown_command.py:22, git_checkout.py:19 - helper-process pipe reads, not Command properties).

Non-path environment reads are NOT emitted: os.environ.get('THEFUCK_INSTANT_MODE') bash.py:38 / zsh.py:41, os.environ.get('TF_SHELL') shells/__init__.py:24, os.environ.get('TF_SHELL_ALIASES') bash.py:64 / zsh.py:69, os.environ.get('PYTHONIOENCODING') types.py:260, os.environ.get('SHELL') entrypoints/shell_logger.py:70 (feeds os.execlp - command channel), os.environ.get('TF_ALIAS') utils.py:304, THEFUCK_OVERRIDDEN_ALIASES fish.py, dict(os.environ) rerun.py:53 (env copy for the re-executed command). They are mode flags/strings with no path use.
Non-path CLI fields are NOT emitted: known_args.help/version/alias/enable_experimental_instant_mode (main.py:20-:28), args.yes/debug/repeat in conf.py:_settings_from_args (:115-127) - boolean flags.

Path-construction by string concatenation: brew_unknown_command.py builds tap/cmd paths with `+` (brew_path_prefix + BREW_CMD_PATH, :14/:27/:33/:37) instead of os.path.join/Path - these concatenations are not matched by any call-shape family; the resulting os.listdir/os.path.isdir calls (:17/:36/:38/:49/:50) ARE emitted as sink rows, so the access site is covered even though the construction node is not.

mmap.mmap(fd, ...) at entrypoints/shell_logger.py:76 and read_log.py:94 is NOT emitted: argument 0 is an integer fd (the path is consumed upstream at the paired os.open row), and the sink core per the task contract is the controlled PATH parameter of actual filesystem operations - the fd rows would be pure duplicates of the os.open rows.

os.write(fd, ...) entrypoints/shell_logger.py:75, f.write(data) :17, f.move/f.seek/f.write :20-:23, and history_file.readlines()/write() bodies are content I/O on already-open handles - not path parameters; not emitted.

os.getcwd()/os.getcwdu() (cd_correction.py:47/:49) are path ORIGINS (cwd), not attacker-controlled path inputs; they are recorded here. The cwd is then joined with spell-corrected script_parts segments at :58.

Pure string operations are not emitted: path.strip('"') utils.py:65, .as_posix() utils.py:214/:255, str(...) coercions, .split(os.sep) cd_correction.py:40, .replace operations in rules; shell.and_/or_ command string assembly is command-construction, not path construction.

Popen family (rerun.py:60 Popen(expanded, shell=True), the Popen(['bash'...]) version probes in shells/*, subprocess helper rules like apt_invalid_operation.py:43, dnf_no_such_command.py:23, docker_not_command.py:22, git_checkout.py:16, brew prefix check_output) are command-execution channels (Pass 2), not path traversal; not emitted.
os.execlp(shell, shell) entrypoints/shell_logger.py:42 - command execution channel, not emitted.

Shell-configuration paths (bash.py:76-84, zsh.py:86-88, fish.py:105-109, tcsh.py:41-43) are literal operator-owned strings; the Path(path).expanduser().exists() check at generic.py:154 and the open('r')/open('a') at not_configured.py:78/:85 are emitted as sink rows, but no source row is emitted for configuration_details.path (not attacker-controlled).

Conditional platform branch: system/__init__.py imports win32 on sys.platform == 'win32' else unix - both files' Path monkey-patches (Path.expanduser = _expanduser) are extracted as .expanduser member CALL rows only where calls exist; the monkey-patch assignments themselves are not flow nodes.
